events.title: Hispanic Heritage Month 2026
events.description:
Hispanic Heritage Month 2026
“Unidos Somos Más — Together We Are More!”

Join the Stony Brook University community as we celebrate 37 years of Hispanic Heritage Month at SBU!

From September 15 through November 6, we invite students, faculty, staff, departments, student organizations, and community partners to celebrate the rich cultures, histories, identities, achievements, and contributions of Latine communities.

This year’s theme, “Unidos Somos Más — Together We Are More!”, reflects the strength and possibilities that emerge when we come together, share our stories, celebrate our wide range of identities, and build meaningful connections. The Hispanic Heritage Month Committee, DICE, and campus partners will offer a variety of cultural, educational, social, and community-building programs for the Stony Brook community.

Whether you are a department, student organization, faculty or staff member, or community partner, we invite you to take part in HHM 2026. Attend a signature event, support a student organization, learn something new, share your culture, or host an event or initiative of your own. Every contribution helps make Hispanic Heritage Month a more vibrant and inclusive reflection of our community.

Whether through the arts, music and food, cultural traditions, meaningful dialogue, educational programs, academic/research opportunities, career networking, awards and scholarships, civic engagement, or simply connecting, there are many ways to celebrate, participate, and be part of HHM. 

For event details and the full Hispanic Heritage Month 2026 calendar, visit www.stonybrook.edu/hhm.

Because when we come together, Unidos Somos Más — Together We Are More!
---

events.title: Garba Eve - Dandiya Raas Utsav
events.description:
Our Garba celebration will bring everyone together to experience the joy and cultural traditions of Navratri. The event will begin with a brief introduction to the significance of Garba, followed by a communal Aarti to honor Goddess Durga, her history, and her values. Participants will have the opportunity to share the floor, dance in unison, and learn about the different ways this rhythmic festival is celebrated across regions. We will also enjoy a variety of traditional festive foods and sweets in a vibrant and welcoming atmosphere. The celebration aims to promote cultural appreciation, strengthen community bonds, and create a memorable experience filled with togetherness, active learning, and festive spirit.

events.title: USG Club Co-Lab: Religious and Spiritual Organizations
events.description:
USG x SEA Club Co-Lab Series

USG and Student Engagement & Activities invite club leaders to the Club Co-Lab Series, a set of collaborative working sessions organized by club category. Each Co-Lab is designed to help organizations meet relevant partners, share resources, develop joint-event ideas, and leave with practical next steps for collaboration.

Each session will include networking, an icebreaker, a brief USG presentation on funding, treasury information, the Club Closet, and important SEA guidelines, followed by a department-specific resource presentation and interactive collaboration activities. Clubs will take part in activities such as Resources Bingo, scenario planning, and a “Build Your Own Event” challenge that helps them identify potential partners and turn an idea into a feasible program.

USG will also collect feedback and follow up on collaboration commitments so that these conversations lead to real partnerships, shared programming, and stronger support for clubs throughout the year. Attendees will have the opportunity to win snacks and gift-card incentives.

We strongly encourage each organization to send at least two representatives, ideally members of the club’s Core Four: President, Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer.

Club Co-Lab Schedule

September 14: Sports Clubs
September 16: Academic and Honor Societies
September 28: Cultural Organizations
September 30: Activism and Advocacy Organizations
October 19: Religious and Spiritual Organizations
October 21: Leisure Activities Organizations
October 28: Community Awareness and Service Organizations
November 4: Performance Clubs
November 10: Media Organizations

Unless otherwise indicated on the individual event page, sessions will be held in Student Activities Center (SAC) 302. Please attend the session that best fits your organization’s primary category.

events.title: Town Hall
events.description:
This event is a town hall for various Democratic candidates running on Long Island. A town hall is a type of debate format in which moderators (SBU Dems students) will be asking a question to the candidates, who will then answer in turn with an even speaking time allotted to each of them. We will have a buzzer and helpers who will let candidates know when their time is running out. The candidates will be arraigned in a semi circle format center stage in chairs, with a table on the side for moderators and timekeepers. After all questions are asked by the moderators (1hr30min-2hr), we will open up the floor to the crowd for a Q/A period (30-45 minutes), where moderators will bring the mic to students raising their hands, and let them ask their question. We will also have someone outside helping check people in and directing them where to go. The first row or two will most likely be reserved for campaign staff on site. There will also be a photographer within our Club, taking photos of the event.  This event will be open to all students / staff , regardless of political affiliation or membership of any clubs. This is a great opportunity for people to get to know their candidates, and ask their representatives the questions they have. The name of the candidates is as follows

Chris Gallant
Former County Executive Pat Halpin

Congresswoman Laura Gillen
Assemblywoman Rebecca Kassay
Chris Murray
Craig Herskowitz 
Trish Kopp
Lynn Trupiano-O'Keefe

Moderators

Photographer(s)

events.title: Bioethics Society: Cryonics & Taxidermy
events.description:
Join the Bioethics Society for a thought-provoking GBM exploring cryonics, taxidermy, and the ethics of preserving the body after death. We’ll discuss why people choose different forms of preservation, from freezing human remains in hopes that future technology may one day restore life to preserving animals through taxidermy for scientific, cultural, memorial, or artistic purposes.

Students will consider questions surrounding death, bodily autonomy, consent, dignity, scientific advancement, and the meaning of preservation. Is it ethical to preserve a human body in the hope of future revival? Should individuals have complete control over what happens to their bodies after death? Does preserving an animal through taxidermy honor it, or can it be considered disrespectful? We’ll also examine how cultural and personal beliefs can shape the way people view death and preservation.

The meeting will include interactive scenarios and open discussion where students can share their perspectives and respond to different ethical dilemmas. No prior knowledge of bioethics, cryonics, or taxidermy is needed, just come ready to discuss some unusual and fascinating questions about life, death, and what happens afterward.

events.title: College Teaching Seminar 2: From Expert Bias to Clear Instruction: Insights from the Learning Sciences
events.description:
The College Teaching Seminars welcomes graduate students and postdocs with a series of interactive 1.5-hour sessions throughout the academic year on relevant topics in college teaching. 

We will explore strategies for creating an inclusive and effective learning environment where students feel they belong and can succeed. Topics covered include building positive relationships with students, making inclusive course design choices, using engaging teaching methods, and fostering a growth mindset. This interactive session will guide you to reflect on your own learning experiences and brainstorm ways to apply inclusive practices.

events.title: USG Club Co-Lab: Leisure Activities Organizations
events.description:
USG x SEA Club Co-Lab Series

USG and Student Engagement & Activities invite club leaders to the Club Co-Lab Series, a set of collaborative working sessions organized by club category. Each Co-Lab is designed to help organizations meet relevant partners, share resources, develop joint-event ideas, and leave with practical next steps for collaboration.

Each session will include networking, an icebreaker, a brief USG presentation on funding, treasury information, the Club Closet, and important SEA guidelines, followed by a department-specific resource presentation and interactive collaboration activities. Clubs will take part in activities such as Resources Bingo, scenario planning, and a “Build Your Own Event” challenge that helps them identify potential partners and turn an idea into a feasible program.

USG will also collect feedback and follow up on collaboration commitments so that these conversations lead to real partnerships, shared programming, and stronger support for clubs throughout the year. Attendees will have the opportunity to win snacks and gift-card incentives.

We strongly encourage each organization to send at least two representatives, ideally members of the club’s Core Four: President, Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer.

Club Co-Lab Schedule

September 14: Sports Clubs
September 16: Academic and Honor Societies
September 28: Cultural Organizations
September 30: Activism and Advocacy Organizations
October 19: Religious and Spiritual Organizations
October 21: Leisure Activities Organizations
October 28: Community Awareness and Service Organizations
November 4: Performance Clubs
November 10: Media Organizations

Unless otherwise indicated on the individual event page, sessions will be held in Student Activities Center (SAC) 302. Please attend the session that best fits your organization’s primary category.

Location: Staller Center Recital Hall
Tickets: Free

Stony Brook Contemporary Chamber Players open the new season with a classic of the American avant-garde and a world premiere, in a concert of works inspired by and responding to the natural world. The program includes George Crumb's theatrical 1971 masterpiece Vox Balaenae (For Three Masked Players), inspired by the singing of the humpback whale; the world premiere of Stony Brook professor Matthew Barnson's Morningside Variations, his response to his New York neighborhood's transition from winter into spring; graduate student composer Conrad Foreman's new version of his Snow and Smokestacks, inspired by a winter's observation of snow falling as smoke rose; and two new songs from graduate student Jake Ellzey's band Lot 40.

events.title: Birth and Evolution of LLMs Part 1
events.description:
In this workshop, we will take a historical journey through the ideas that eventually led to today’s large language models, such as ChatGPT and Claude. Modern LLMs can seem overwhelmingly complex, but they didn't appear all at once. Many of the basic ideas behind them have been developing for more than a century. By following this history step by step, we can better understand what language models do and how they evolved. In part 1 of this workshop, we will begin with Andrey Markov’s early work on sequences and probability in 1913 and Claude Shannon’s influential work on information and language in 1948. From there, we will explore key ideas such as Markov chains, N-grams, and the next-word generation process using simple, accessible examples. In part 2, date to be determined, we will also look at how an artificial neuron can learn to predict the next word, an important step toward neural language models that later became the foundation of modern LLMs and we will see what perplexity is. The workshop is designed for anyone who is curious about where today’s AI came from and how a century of ideas about language, probability, and computation helped make modern language models possible. This workshop targets students of any level who are interested in language models or history. No background in computer science or artificial intelligence is required. The hardest part is converting counted numbers to probabilities. Our historical journey will cover roughly the period from 1918 to 1970s.

events.description:
The Beer Goggles Challenge is an activity designed to simulate the effects of alcohol impairment. Participants wear specially designed goggles that distort vision and coordination, mimicking the sensation of being intoxicated. During the challenge, students attempt simple tasks like walking in a straight line, picking up objects, or navigating obstacles. The goal is to demonstrate how alcohol impairs judgment, reaction time, and motor skills, reinforcing the dangers of driving under the influence or engaging in risky behaviors while intoxicated. It provides a hands-on, impactful learning experience about the real-world consequences of alcohol impairment.
Dress Code: Casual (jeans ok)

events.title: To God’s Ear: A Film Screening
events.description:
Filmed on the North Fork of Long Island, To God’s Ear is an independent film by veteran director and writer Stan Schofield about trauma, grief, resilience, and the healing power of connection.

The film follows the unlikely friendship between two teenage girls who face trauma and loss as they learn to trust one another and find healing through their bond with a special horse. Their journey brings together two grieving families searching for hope and redemption as they explore the unique bond between humans and horses and the potential of equine therapy to support healing.

Free for students, faculty, and staff. Click link to register: https://forms.gle/rPw1drS5z3HkxrHEA

events.title: University Affairs Committee Meeting
events.description:
The University Affairs Committee serves as a space for undergraduate students to raise concerns, discuss campus-wide issues, and work on initiatives that improve the student experience at Stony Brook University. Led by the Vice President of University Affairs, the committee focuses on areas such as academic policies, accessibility, transportation and parking, campus technology, student services, and other university-wide concerns.

Committee members work together to gather student feedback, develop advocacy initiatives, research potential policy solutions, and communicate student concerns to university administrators and shared governance bodies. The committee also helps strengthen undergraduate representation within University governance and provides students with an opportunity to become directly involved in creating positive change on campus.

All undergraduate students are welcome to attend, share concerns, propose ideas, and get involved in University Affairs initiatives.

events.title: Medical Mystery
events.description:
Medical Mystery is an interactive, team-based event in which students work together to investigate and solve a fictional patient case inspired by real-world medical and global health scenarios. The event is designed to introduce students to clinical reasoning, differential diagonosis, teamwork, and evidentce-bsed decision-making while demonstrating how healthcare professionals use multiple pisces of patient information to determine a possible diagnosis and treatment plan. Each each will receive a patient file containing symptoms, medical history, travel, or exposure history, and other initil information. Throughout the event, teams will unlock additional clues such as vital signs, lab results, physical examination findings, and diagnostic information to narrow down possible conditions. Teams will submit a final diagnosis and explain their reasoning before the correct diagnosis, treatment, and relevant health information are revealed. A small prize may be awared to the team that correclty sovles the case.

events.title: Relating Majors to Minors w/ The Career Center!
events.description:
Myth: A student's major ties them to a specific career path. 
Truth: While some majors help students develop specialized skills, most people end up working in careers that are not directly related to their major. 

What employers really value are the career-life skills that can be developed through a variety of majors. This module focuses on how to connect majors of interest to possible career paths. We explore strategies for deciding on a major and tools to identify related careers.

Join us learn the following:

Describe the relationship between majors and careers
Identify three strategies for exploring majors and careers of interest
Develop a plan to explore a career area of interest

events.title: NMDP x SBU Biweekly Tabling
events.description:
NMDP x SBU is the stony brook chapter of NMDP, an international non-profit dedicated to supporting blood stem cell donation. Blood stem cell donation is a curative treatment for blood disorders including but not limited to leukemia, lymphoma and sickle cell anemia. The limitation to blood stem cell donation is that the donor and recipient must be a genetic match to ensure the patient's body does not reject the donation. Due to wide genetic diversity, it is extremely difficult for searching patients to find a genetic match, but with every new member of the registry, a patient's chance increases. Our tabling is focused on both education and recruitment for the stony brook university community!

events.title: USG Club Co-Lab: Community Awareness and Service Organizations
events.description:
USG x SEA Club Co-Lab Series

USG and Student Engagement & Activities invite club leaders to the Club Co-Lab Series, a set of collaborative working sessions organized by club category. Each Co-Lab is designed to help organizations meet relevant partners, share resources, develop joint-event ideas, and leave with practical next steps for collaboration.

Each session will include networking, an icebreaker, a brief USG presentation on funding, treasury information, the Club Closet, and important SEA guidelines, followed by a department-specific resource presentation and interactive collaboration activities. Clubs will take part in activities such as Resources Bingo, scenario planning, and a “Build Your Own Event” challenge that helps them identify potential partners and turn an idea into a feasible program.

USG will also collect feedback and follow up on collaboration commitments so that these conversations lead to real partnerships, shared programming, and stronger support for clubs throughout the year. Attendees will have the opportunity to win snacks and gift-card incentives.

We strongly encourage each organization to send at least two representatives, ideally members of the club’s Core Four: President, Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer.

Club Co-Lab Schedule

September 14: Sports Clubs
September 16: Academic and Honor Societies
September 28: Cultural Organizations
September 30: Activism and Advocacy Organizations
October 19: Religious and Spiritual Organizations
October 21: Leisure Activities Organizations

events.title: Christina Dahl and Jennifer Frautschi Faculty Recital
events.description:
Date and Time: Wednesday, October 28, 2026, 7:00 pm
Location: Staller Center Recital Hall
Tickets: $56 to $60

Acclaimed Stony Brook Music faculty members Jennifer Frautschi, violin, and Christina Dahl, piano, perform a program of musical rarities: two 19th-century gems paired with two rare 20th-century voices. They begin the program with Beethoven’s Violin Sonata No. 4 and end the program with Saint-Saëns Violin Sonata No. 1. In between, travel on a musical journey from Elgar's nostalgic warmth to the virtuosity and intensity of Schoenberg's rhapsodic Phantasy. 

Program:
Beethoven Violin Sonata No. 4 in A minor, Op. 23
Elgar Violin Sonata in E minor, Op. 82
Schoenberg Phantasy for Violin with Piano Accompaniment, Op. 47
Saint-Saëns Violin Sonata No. 1 in D minor, Op. 75


Dress Code: Casual (jeans ok)

events.title: DIY Bird Feeders Community Service Event
events.description:
Delta Sigma Pi will be hosting a DIY Bird Feeder Crafting Event focused on environmental awareness and wildlife conservation. The event will begin with a brief presentation discussing environmental issues and their impact on local wildlife, particularly birds and their habitats. Following the presentation, participants will create bird feeders using pine cones, birdseed, animal-friendly peanut butter, and string.

This hands-on activity aims to encourage environmental responsibility, creativity, and community engagement while educating participants on simple ways to support local wildlife. Participants will be able to take their completed bird feeders home and hang them in suitable outdoor spaces to help provide food for birds.
Dress Code: Casual (jeans ok)

events.title: Running Club Practice
events.description:
Practice is Monday-Friday @ 4:00 pm at the University Track. We will meet at the Rec Center instead if the weather is bad.

The purpose of the running club is to unite runners of all abilities for the common goal of bettering their individual fitness. Accommodations will be made for everyone in the Stony Brook campus community. This club will be held five days per week, but people may come when they can since schedules vary. In addition to weekday practices, we will attend meets on various weekends throughout the semester, which are completely optional. This group will be good for people looking to meet new friends, stay in shape, have a healthier lifestyle, as well as compete in a setting that is more relaxed than a Division 1 sports team. Overall, the goal is for everyone to try their best and have fun.

Search for our club on Discord, Facebook, Instagram, and Strava to get connected virtually!
